top3.headline: Claude joins your team's video calls
top3.whyItMatters: Your meetings become agent context; decide now what Claude may record and reuse.

top3.headline: Anthropic lets you host its agents in your own cloud
top3.whyItMatters: Data-sensitive teams lose one big reason to wait on agents.

top3.headline: Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen bets on speed
top3.whyItMatters: Faster models change the cost of everyday agent work; retest your defaults.

items.title: Perplexity open-sources Decider v1.3 decision models
items.takeaway: Decider v1.3 and Decider Flash v1.3 add a 'locate' capability and are free on OpenRouter for a week.
items.soWhat: Small open decision models are a cheap option for routing and classification inside agents.

items.title: Replit Agent can now buy ads for your business
items.takeaway: Replit's CEO says users can ask the agent to make purchases, including ads to acquire customers.
items.soWhat: Agents now spend company money; set budgets, approvals and audit trails before turning this on.

items.title: Anthropic puts Claude inside your team's video calls
items.takeaway: Claude Meetings joins video calls and builds docs and whiteboards live; beta on Team and Enterprise plans.
items.soWhat: Meetings become a source of agent context; set rules for what Claude may hear and keep.

items.title: Cursor: Gemini 4 Hydrogen scores 54.3% on CursorBench
items.takeaway: Up from 39.6% for Gemini 3.8 Flash at default effort; now available in Cursor.
items.soWhat: A vendor benchmark shows a large jump; check it against your own coding tasks before switching.

items.title: Google ships Gemini 4 Hydrogen, built for speed
items.takeaway: Google says it finishes tasks 2.5x faster than 3.8 Flash and beats Argon on an intelligence index.
items.soWhat: Fast, cheaper models keep improving; retest your default model for everyday agent work.

items.title: Claude Managed Agents can now run in your own cloud
items.takeaway: Private beta: host the agent harness, sandboxes and session history on your cloud or on-premises.
items.soWhat: Regulated teams can run Anthropic's agents while keeping data and logs inside their walls.

items.title: Muse can now make phone calls on your behalf
items.takeaway: Alexandr Wang says Muse now calls insurers, cable firms, the DMV and restaurants for paid US users.
items.soWhat: Agents now reach businesses by voice; expect them on your customer service lines soon.

items.title: Meng To builds a scroll-driven landing page from one video take
items.takeaway: One 30-second HeyGen Video 1 take plays in reverse on scroll; he shares workflow, prompts and a template.
items.soWhat: Rich landing pages no longer need a 3D team; one prompted video can carry the story.

items.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, effective immediately
items.takeaway: Nvidia's newsroom announced a CEO transition; Reuters live coverage reports Huang resigned immediately.
items.soWhat: Your biggest AI supplier changes leaders mid-boom; watch for shifts in pricing, roadmap and allocation.

items.title: Anthropic files its IPO registration with the SEC
items.takeaway: Anthropic says it has filed a registration statement, including a prospectus, for its initial public offering.
items.soWhat: A public Anthropic will disclose costs and risks; read the prospectus before your next model contract.

items.title: Matt Pocock: one Home Repo to run agents across all repos
items.takeaway: He publishes the Home Repo pattern for multi-repo agent work, with a setup prompt to run on your org's repos.
items.soWhat: Agents stall at repo boundaries; a single home repo gives them one map of your whole codebase.

items.title: Naval: someone, somewhere, will build the datacenters
items.takeaway: He calls datacenters a globally competitive market and says someone, somewhere, will build them.
items.soWhat: Compute supply is global; local limits shift where capacity lands, not whether it exists.

items.title: Meng To shares a full tutorial for his three.js apartment
items.takeaway: He walks through recreating his apartment in three.js with Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.2.
items.soWhat: Designers can now ship interactive 3D with agents; a tutorial makes it repeatable for teams.

items.title: United won't let unauthorized AI agents book flights
items.takeaway: The Verge reports United is refusing bookings made by unauthorized AI agents.
items.soWhat: Agent access is now a business decision; check which partners will block your customer-facing agents.

items.title: AI agent web traffic grew 8x from August to October
items.takeaway: a16z cites HUMAN Security; The Verge reports United won't let AI agents book flights.
items.soWhat: Decide now whether agents are customers you serve or traffic you block.

related.name: a16z: Welcome to the B2A Economy

items.title: a16z: H100 rental rates run 54% above expected depreciation
items.takeaway: As of Oct 19, A100s sat 9% and H100s 54% above a six-year straight-line path.
items.soWhat: Compute keeps its value longer than planned, so budget for rental prices staying high.

items.title: Perplexity: general models beat cyber models at breaking its agent sandbox
items.takeaway: Red-teaming SPACE, GPT 5.6 Sol found exploits better than GPT 5.6 Sol Cyber.
items.soWhat: Test agent sandboxes with your strongest general model, not only specialist security tools.

items.title: Google launches an API that scores 1,000 choices in one pass
items.takeaway: Gemini Decision 1 picks from closed sets across text, images, audio, video and PDFs.
items.soWhat: Triage, tagging and routing are closed-set choices; test whether this beats your current setup.

items.title: VulnCheck: Glasswing logged 37,966 findings, only 217 marked fixed
items.takeaway: It counts 442 CVEs tied to Anthropic, two exploited; curl rejected 19 of 34 scanner reports.
items.soWhat: AI finds bugs faster than people can verify and fix them, so budget for triage.

items.title: Lyn Alden: wary of Huang's tenure, bullish on 2027 GPU demand
items.takeaway: She calls herself neutral to bearish on Huang as CEO and bullish on GPU demand in 2027.
items.soWhat: A respected macro voice separates Nvidia's leadership risk from the demand for AI compute.

items.title: Nathan Benaich: defenders need open cyber models too
items.takeaway: He says Hugging Face found API guardrails slowed an intrusion probe and used a self-hosted open model.
items.soWhat: Closed-model guardrails can block your own security team; keep an open-model option for incidents.

hotOnX.text: Introducing Claude Meetings: add Claude to your team's video call and it builds docs, whiteboards, and other artifacts with you.
hotOnX.note: An AI teammate in live meetings is the day's most watched launch.

hotOnX.text: Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents is now in private beta.
hotOnX.note: Builders want agents that run where their data already lives.

hotOnX.text: Meet Gemini 4 Hydrogen: built for rapid coding, multimodal synthesis, and everyday workflows.
hotOnX.note: A fast new Gemini lands a day after Theo found Gemini 4 Carbon slow.

hotOnX.text: Gemini 4 Hydrogen is now available in Cursor! At its default effort, it scores 54.3% on CursorBench.
hotOnX.note: Developers get a quick benchmark to judge the new model.

hotOnX.text: New video: how we launch new models on our API, and how to measure cost per task when you upgrade.
hotOnX.note: Teams want a method for model upgrades, not just new models.
